topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the core learning objectives regarding cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss standard interventions including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, as well as the physiological challenges and resistance mechanisms associated with non-targeted treatments.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies designed to exploit specific intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities, including hormone dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Small-molecule kinase inhibitors and resistance pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on the mechanism of small-molecule inhibitors targeting oncogenic kinases and the molecular pathways driving resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe antibody-based therapeutic modalities used to block surface receptors, engage cytotoxic effector mechanisms, or deliver targeted toxic payloads to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and engineered T-cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and methods for re-engaging or engineering T cells to destroy cancer cells.

topics.label: Overall progress, clinical dilemmas, and future perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize broad trends in cancer mortality, evaluating the interplay between therapeutic advances, screening, ethical dilemmas, and future directions in patient management.
